text:
Good evening, Burlington. Sunset comes at 4:25, and with the clouds still locked in, don't expect much of a show. The light will just fade to gray a little after 4. It's holding around 40 right now and will ease to a low near 38 tonight. That's a few degrees milder than it might have been, since the clouds and the northwest breeze keep the temperature from dropping much. The roads and sidewalks should stay above freezing, so I'm not worried about ice.

Monday looks a lot like today: cloudy, dry, and chilly, with a high near 42. Some forecasts hint at afternoon breaks in the clouds, but I'd bet on gray most of the day. Skies clear Monday night and it gets colder, near 31, so expect a little frost Tuesday morning.

Tuesday is the turn. It's sunny with a high near 50, and the 50s hang around through the week. Wear the warm jacket tomorrow, and leave the umbrella home.

week.blurb: Cloudy and chilly, high near 44; the official forecast has no rain, but the European model sees showers, so pack an umbrella.
Gray and cold again with a high near 42, but it clears overnight and turns frosty, with lows around 31.
Sunny and a good 8 degrees warmer than Monday, with a high near 50; a nice day to get outside.
Mostly sunny and mild with a high near 55, a nice November stretch if the pattern holds.
Mostly sunny again, high near 54, with the mild stretch looking like it holds and a light south breeze.
Looks like partly sunny and mild, high near 55, with clouds building a bit by evening.
Looks like a mostly sunny Saturday with a high near 54, then a breezier, cloudier night.

AFD KEY MESSAGES (forecaster's reasoning, issued 2026-11-15T19:14:00+00:00 — covers the whole BTV area, northern NY included: translate to what Burlington feels, never repeat other regions' place names):
  1. After upslope snow showers/flurries at elevations above 1500 feet or so gradually wind down tonight, a dry period will begin areawide. Seasonably cool and cloudy conditions into Monday will trend sunny on Tuesday as a warming trend begins.
  2. Warm and dry weather will persist through mid to late week.
AFD WHAT CHANGED (same regional caveat): As of 214 PM EST Sunday... Nighttime temperatures are a few to several degrees milder for tonight and tomorrow night in most locations.
AFD DISCUSSION (the forecaster's full reasoning, same regional caveat; their temps are area-wide ranges):
KEY MESSAGE 1: Light snow showers in the Adirondacks, northern Greens, and northeastern highlands in Vermont have persisted into early afternoon. Water vapor imagery shows an additional shortwave to our north pivoting towards northeastern Vermont which should keep slightly higher chances of showers in this region into the evening. To the west, decreasing radar returns nearer to KTYX show cloud tops have warmed/lowered, and there are some increasing breaks in the clouds cover per webcams and satellite imagery. Overall, this suggests further upslope precipitation will trend lighter and more intermittent; expect no travel impacts given these precipitation rates and increasingly localized precipitation. Also, while wet roads often leads to risk of ice formation at night, persistent northwest flow and cloud layer will prevent radiative cooling that is needed for more substantial surface temperature falls. In fact, based on recent temperature verification and this cloudy and breezy pattern, we went closer to raw model guidance and away from bias-corrected and more climatological overnight temperatures. As such, think most lower elevation spots will see low temperatures only bottom out near or slightly above freezing rather than well below freezing. While increasingly anti-cyclonic flow will lead to dry weather on Monday, low level moisture will be trapped due to strong subsidence. As a result, persistent cloud cover just about areawide will be likely through the day as winds remain out of the northwest. This cloudiness will limit mixing depth and heating, so it will be one more day with seasonably chilly daytime temperatures in the upper 30s to mid 40s despite rising temperatures aloft. In contrast, on Tuesday as the center of a large ridge of high pressure to our southwest migrates nearer and low level flow becomes southwesterly, we should scatter the shallow cloud cover with a mainly sunny sky for most of the day anticipated. The combination of a moderating air mass and sunshine should lead to the first in a series of days with high temperatures at least 10 degrees above normal. KEY MESSAGE 2: A ridge of high pressure will remain entrenched across much of the eastern CONUS for the latter half of this week. The result will be a continued period of dry weather. A series of shortwave troughs/frontal systems will attempt to break down the ridge late in the week toward next weekend. However, the ridge looks to hold firm, shunting northern stream systems to our north, with perhaps a glancing blow along the international border on Friday. Models have some consensus in better chances for precipitation later next weekend, but there's not much agreement in deterministic or ensemble guidance in exactly how things would play out. In addition to the dry weather, temperatures will remain above normal, particularly during the day when highs in the 50s will be common (low to mid 40s is normal for mid November). WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): BURLINGTON, Vt. (WCAX) - Mt. Mansfield received around 4 inches of snow on Saturday, marking the latest date to receive an inch of snow or greater. This breaks the previous record of November 9th, 1985. A general 1 to 4 inches of snow fell in the region, mainly in the mountains. This system responsible for this is moving out, so only scattered valley sprinkles and mountain flurries are expected, mainly this morning. It will remain mostly cloudy and a bit blustery through the afternoon with highs in the upper 30s to low 40s. The week will have a return to an extended period of dry and mild weather, similar to what we’ve had in October. Monday will be partly sunny with highs in the 40s. Tuesday through Thursday will have plenty of sunshine with highs mainly in the 50s. Some upper 50s are possible by Thursday, so any snow will melt through the week. A weak cold front may touch off an isolated shower on Friday, otherwise there’s the possibility for the dry stretch to continue into next weekend.
NBC5 METEOROLOGIST (2026-11-15T13:59:00Z — same caveat): Drier Sunday, but staying chilly with lots of clouds — Sunday stays mostly cloudy and chilly, with highs in the low 40s. Expect a few lingering mixed showers in the morning, followed by a mostly dry afternoon. Southern Vermont can expect more breaks of sun. Tonight will be mostly cloudy and seasonably cold, with lows in the 20s and 30s. Clouds will be stubborn on Monday, though many towns should see a gradual clearing trend through the afternoon. Highs again reach the low 40s. Tuesday marks the transition toward brighter and warmer weather. Expect a partly to mostly sunny sky, with highs near 50. The Wednesday through Friday stretch looks beautiful, with partly sunny skies and highs reaching the mid to upper 50s. The mild and quiet pattern continues next weekend. Highs reach well into the 50s, with plenty of sun. A cooler, more seasonable airmass likely returns Thanksgiving week as highs fall back to the 40s. A few rain and snow showers are possible as a front passes through.
